page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. The system features 48 dedicated physical cores running on AWS Graviton2 processors (Neoverse-N1) clocked at 2.5 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 96.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard compute-optimized 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For I/O performance, the instance includes 2850 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local instance storage and delivers a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight strong scaling in highly parallel environments, evidenced by a top-quartile stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 72,845.21. However, single-core processing demonstrates lower efficiency, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression landing in the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth metrics sit in the middle 50%, registering 148.11 GB/sec on large read blocks and 71.03 GB/sec on write blocks. The server handles intermediate workloads effectively, reaching 54.64 million operations per second on Redis SET operations and 39.7 GB/sec in static web serving.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on the ARMv8 instruction set, which provides hardware-accelerated AES cryptography but lacks x86-specific SIMD instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX. This limits compute throughput for legacy vector algorithms, single-threaded processing, and large LLM prompt processing. Conversely, the high density of dedicated physical cores paired with 2850 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage provides strong resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out applications.

Amazon Web Services c6gd.12xlarge is suited for multi-threaded, parallelized tasks that demand low-latency local scratch space. Primary workload fits include batch processing, distributed data pipelines, CI/CD compilation farms, containerized microservices, and high-throughput caching tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud server driven by 48 dedicated physical cores of 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 (Neoverse-N1) processors running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core), 2850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and 20 Gbps baseline networking on the Nitro hypervisor. Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute scaling alongside moderate memory bandwidth and average static web serving throughput. However, single-core throughput is constrained, and the ARM architecture lacks x86 vector extensions like AVX-512. The pairing of 48 physical execution cores and high-speed local storage makes this server well positioned for parallel batch workloads, software compilation, caching, and data processing.
